text:
Alice M.: seeing weird sustained throughput drop on gpu-pool-west-2-slot-b starting ~10:12 UTC, p99 tokens tripled, tail latencies spiky.
Ben K.: any config changes rolled out around then?
Alice M.: we did push qos-shaper v2 to the west AZs at 10:05, but that was supposed to be a safe tweak.
Carol S.: could be burst-budget starvation on that slice — traffic pattern had a sudden fanout from a batch of small requests.
Dana R.: infra-bot just fired: [ALERT] pool_degraded gpu-pool-west-2-slot-b 10:13 UTC (err: route_drop_rate>5%).
infra-bot: alert_id=pgw-west2-1943210000, runbook: https://internal/runbooks/pool-degraded
Ben K.: can someone grep the nic counters? suspect egress queue 1 saturating and the router is dropping instead of shaping.
Alice M.: running quick probe against node exporter on a host: ```curl -s http://10.12.45.7:9100/metrics | egrep 'tx_packets|tx_dropped' | tail -n5``` got `tx_dropped{dev="eth0"} 1345` on the offending host.
Carol S.: that aligns. If kernel qdisc is dropping at host, our service-level routing may be unaware and continues to send to that slot — creating a routing blackhole.
Dana R.: temporary mitigation: can we flip pool routing to prefer pool-b-standby for new allocs? small CLI: `rictl route modify --pool gpu-pool-west-2 --prefer standby`
Ben K.: doing that now, will route new requests away. note: existing connections will stay on the host until KV cache invalidation.
Alice M.: thanks — after flipping, p50/p99 improved for new traffic but legacy sessions still affected. eviction logs show repeated model reloads: `OOM when allocating tensor` followed by preempt attempts.
Carol S.: sounds like a GPU memory thrash from a high-concurrency tenant causing lane-hogging. propose: add a short-term per-tenant cap on concurrent contexts for that pool and increase the pool's burst tokens.
Dana R.: agree. policy change: `tenant_cap.concurrency=12` for tenant:marketing-experiments on that pool + bump pool burst to 2x. I can push a canary in 5m.
Ben K.: cost note: doubling burst tokens increases risk of overprovisioning; ops budget ok for a few hours while we stabilize.
Alice M.: rolling canary now. infra-bot: annotate the incident with runbook step we performed and tag customers affected.
infra-bot: incident updated: mitigation_step=route_prefer_standby, canary_started_by=Alice M., status=investigating
Dana R.: after canary, tail latency for affected sessions dropped ~35% and dropped packets on the host decreased.
Carol S.: follow-ups: 1) add exporter alert for host-level tx_dropped > 1000 in 5m, 2) model-scheduler: enforce soft per-tenant concurrency cap per-pool, 3) run failure-mode sim in staging to validate graceful fallback.
Alice M.: filing a short RFC for the scheduler change and adding a postmortem entry later today. thanks all. :thumbsup:
